The problem
Most traders are flying blind
By the time news breaks, the price has already moved. — the public feels informed right when the edge is gone
The people who actually move these markets are anonymous wallets. — no name, no face, no track record — unless you know where to look
Without a way to see size flowing in, you're reacting to price. — instead of reacting to information
You are not competing with other retail traders. You're competing with wallets that have already done the research.

Module 1
How a prediction-market contract works
Each contract pays $1 if the event happens, $0 if it doesn't.
The price IS the market's implied probability. — a contract priced at 58 cents means the market thinks there's a 58% chance
Kalshi is CFTC-regulated and cash-settled in the US.
Polymarket runs on-chain, globally, through pseudonymous crypto wallets.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
06 / 47
Module 1
Polymarket's superpower: everything is public
Every wallet, every trade, every position size sits on the blockchain. — permanently, and visible the second it's confirmed
You don't need insider access or a Bloomberg terminal. — you need the right lens on data that's already public
That lens is what VisibleTrader is built to be.
On a stock exchange, order flow like this is exactly what a hedge fund pays for. On Polymarket, it's sitting in the open.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook

A historically profitable wallet suddenly taking a big new position is information. — not proof — information

Module 2
How to read a signal like an analyst
Size — is this large relative to the market's liquidity, or a rounding error?
Wallet history — check Leaderboard and Profits before you react to anything
Timing — fresh conviction, or a stale position just now getting noticed?
Market — is this an event you can independently research, or pure noise?
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
15 / 47
Module 2
What ISN'T a real signal
A single trade from an unranked or unprofitable wallet.
A position that's already 90%+ priced in — no edge left to take.
Wash-trade-like patterns: same wallet, opposing markets, no visible thesis.
A size that's large in dollars but tiny relative to that market's volume.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook

Module 3
Why AI Is the Missing Layer
A whale's wallet address is not a thesis. This is where reasoning comes in.

Module 3
Why you can't just copy the whale
You see their position, not their reasoning.
They might be hedging another position you can't see at all.
Even the best-ranked wallets are wrong a meaningful share of the time.
Copying blind turns research into gambling with extra steps.

Step 1 of 5
Spot the signal
Open Signals (or Leaderboard) and note the wallet, market, side, and size.
Check the wallet's rank and record before you feel anything about the trade.
If it fails the Module 2 checklist, stop here — most signals should be discarded.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
23 / 47
Step 2 of 5
Gather real context
Pull the market's exact resolution criteria — how and when it actually settles.
Note the current price and any recent news yourself.
Feed these to Claude as plain facts, not assumptions. — it has no live access, so what you paste in is its entire world
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
24 / 47
Step 3 of 5
State a one-sentence thesis
Prompt: "My thesis is [X]. Here are the three strongest pieces of evidence."
Forces you to commit to reasoning you can test. — not just a vibe borrowed from a whale wallet
If you can't state it in one sentence, you don't have a thesis yet.
Prompt example: "My thesis: [event] resolves YES. Evidence: 1) ... 2) ... 3) ..."
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
25 / 47
Step 4 of 5
Make it argue the other side
The single most useful prompt
"Argue the strongest possible case against my thesis."
If Claude can't build a compelling counter-case, that's a good sign.
If it can — you're not done thinking yet.
Then check your own bias
"Does my reasoning show recency, anchoring, or confirmation bias?"
A cheap gut-check almost nobody runs on themselves.
Takes thirty seconds. Catches the trades you regret.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
26 / 47
Step 5 of 5
Verify the math, then size the trade
Use Kalshi's or Polymarket's own payout calculator for the actual numbers. — not Claude's arithmetic
Reasoning about probability and reasoning about position size are two different skills. — do both, on purpose
Your position size comes from YOUR bankroll rule — never from the whale's dollar amount.

Worked example — part 2 of 3
Thesis vs. counter-case
My thesis
Fed has cut at 3 of the last 3 meetings amid cooling CPI.
Wallet is top-ranked with a 78% win rate over 64 markets.
Size is ~3x this wallet's average bet — real conviction.
Claude's steelman (the other side)
The Fed called future cuts "data dependent" — not settled.
The next CPI print lands 2 days before the meeting.
This wallet's last 3 rate-market trades were all losses.
The counter-case doesn't kill the trade — it surfaces a real risk you now size around.

Module 5
The Strategy Playbook
Eight concrete ways to turn a VisibleTrader signal into a repeatable edge — not just one approach.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
31 / 47
Strategy 1
Leaderboard-Only Entries
Rule — only act on signals from wallets ranked top ~20, with 20+ resolved markets
Why it works — filters out one-off lucky bets and keeps you trading behind proven repeat winners
Watch for — rank can slip after a bad month — recheck it at the time of the signal, not from memory
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
32 / 47
Strategy 2
Size-Weighted Conviction
Rule — compare the trade to that wallet's own average position size from Profits — 3x+ their norm signals real conviction
Why it works — a whale's normal-sized bet is routine; an outsized one means they see something specific
Watch for — don't confuse 'large in dollars' with 'large for them' — a $500K wallet risking $20K is a small bet
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
33 / 47
Strategy 3
Cluster Confirmation
Rule — wait for 2+ independently ranked wallets to take the same side of the same market in a short window
Why it works — independent smart money converging on one outcome beats any single trade as a signal
Watch for — check the wallets aren't linked addresses just moving together — that isn't independence
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
34 / 47
Strategy 4
Distribution / Exit Signal
Rule — treat a top wallet closing or cutting a position as seriously as an entry
Why it works — it's often the first sign the thesis changed — most traders only watch for buys
Watch for — trimming to rebalance risk isn't the same as exiting because they were wrong — check if they zeroed out
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
35 / 47
Strategy 5
Fade the Crowd, Follow the Wallet
Rule — when public price is heavily one-sided but a proven wallet is quietly building the other side, that divergence is worth researching
Why it works — prices often overreact to headlines; track-record wallets are pricing the underlying probability, not the noise
Watch for — the highest-risk strategy here — never skip the Module 4 AI stress-test step on this one
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
36 / 47
Strategy 6
Early-Mover Speed
Rule — act on the Signals feed within the first hour of a large trade confirming, before the public price adjusts
Why it works — the whole edge of on-chain visibility disappears once the crowd catches up
Watch for — speed cuts against Step 2 — set a hard time box (e.g. 20 minutes) so speed doesn't turn into skipping research
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook
37 / 47
Strategy 7
Tiered Conviction Sizing
Rule — set 3 bankroll tiers tied to how many strategies above confirm one trade — 1 signal = 2%, 2 signals = 3.5%, 3+ = 5% cap
Why it works — ties position size to the strength of the evidence, not to how excited you feel
Watch for — write the tiers down before you're looking at a live signal — deciding in the moment defeats the point
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook

Strategy 8
The AI Prompt Playbook
The Steelman Prompt
"Argue the strongest case against my thesis." Run this on every trade, no exceptions.
The Bias Audit
"Does my reasoning show recency, anchoring, or confirmation bias?" A 30-second gut check.
The Resolution Check
"Read this resolution criteria — what's the most likely way this doesn't pay out as I expect?"
The Base-Rate Prompt
"Before the whale's trade, what's the base rate for events like this resolving YES?"

Module 6
Position sizing isn't optional
Decide your risk-per-trade rule before you're excited about a signal — not during.
A common approach: risk a fixed 3–5% of your current bankroll per position, win or lose.
The whale's position size tells you nothing about YOUR position size. — their bankroll and risk tolerance aren't yours
Track every trade in one place so you see your real numbers, not your memory of them.
Vlad's VisibleTrader + AI Playbook

Mistakes that end bankrolls
Chasing a signal after the move already happened.
Sizing up because "the whale went big" instead of following your own plan.
Skipping the counter-argument step when you're excited about a trade.
Treating one win as proof that the system works.

Risk & disclosure
Before you trade a single dollar
This course teaches a research process — how to read on-chain trading data and stress-test a thesis with AI. It is education, not financial advice, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any contract.
Prediction markets carry a real risk of loss. A wallet's past results, including on the VisibleTrader Leaderboard, do not guarantee its next trade will win.
Only trade money you can afford to lose, verify every number yourself before acting, and treat the AI steps in this workflow as a reasoning aid — never as an execution decision on their own.
